title: Script or Module?
prompt: Implement run_report() returning the string 'report'. Then implement the module-level pattern: a variable RAN_DIRECTLY set by the __main__ guard. Because the sandbox imports your code as a module, RAN_DIRECTLY must be False here — and run_report() must not print.
boilerplate:
RAN_DIRECTLY = None

def run_report():
    pass

# add the __main__ guard below

tests.name: run_report returns, does not print
tests.code:
import io, contextlib
buf = io.StringIO()
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buf):
    result = run_report()
assert result == 'report'
assert buf.getvalue() == ''
tests.hint: Return the string; printing would fail this test.

tests.name: guard did not fire on import
tests.hint: if __name__ == '__main__': RAN_DIRECTLY = True — as an imported module, __name__ is not '__main__'.
